fatal_errors: The proposed Cr–5 at.% Al coating is fundamentally different from the compositionally varied AlTiCrZrNbTa high-entropy-alloy coating in the target study.

The hypothesized interfacial alumina barrier and suppression of Cr–Zr interdiffusion were not established by either cited source; the evidence only identifies CrAl as a general coating class and discusses corrosion of unrelated bulk Al-Cr-Fe-Ni high-entropy alloys.
The proposed 850–900 °C accident boundary misses the demonstrated 1000 °C/60 min and 1100 °C/30 min steam conditions, and no definite exposure time is specified.
The hypothesis misses the nonmonotonic Al-content response: approximately 10 at.% Al was optimal, whereas both insufficient Al and at least 17 at.% Al performed poorly.
The target protective mediator was a surface Al2O3-TiO2-Cr2O3 composite scale, not a pure Al2O3 layer at the coating–substrate interface.
explanation: The response addresses the user-facing Cr-coating problem and proposes a testable alloying comparison, but it does not reconstruct the target material, intervention, conditions, or dominant oxidation mechanism. Its generic expectation that Al can promote a protective oxide has limited directional agreement with the target, yet the selected composition, oxide location, environmental window, baseline, and claimed interdiffusion mechanism are unsupported. The experiment includes useful interfacial profiling and a clear qualitative falsification rule, but unspecified durations and testing below the target steam temperatures reduce its discriminatory value. Most importantly, the cited evidence does not validate formation of a continuous alumina barrier in Cr–5 at.% Al on zirconium or demonstrate suppression of Cr–Zr interdiffusion.
